name: Example product-page copy rubric (invented for this demo, not any client's rubric)

categories.name: Title
categories.criteria: Does the title say what the product is, for whom or what it is for, and its key differentiator, in plain words?

levels.0: No usable title, or only a brand name.
levels.1: Title names the product category only; vague or stuffed with keywords.
levels.2: Clear product name but misses either the use or a key attribute.
levels.3: Clear name plus use or key attribute, readable.
levels.4: Clear name, use and a concrete differentiator, natural wording.

categories.name: Benefits and persuasion
categories.criteria: Does the copy explain what the shopper gets (outcomes, situations of use), not only what the product is?

levels.0: No benefits; only a name or a list of nouns.
levels.1: Generic praise with no concrete outcome.
levels.2: Some concrete benefits but most statements are generic.
levels.3: Several concrete benefits tied to real use situations.
levels.4: Benefits are concrete, ordered by importance, and tied to specific features.

categories.name: Structure and scannability
categories.criteria: Can a shopper scan the page? Look at headings, bullets and paragraph length.

levels.2: Some structure (a few bullets or headings) but uneven.
levels.3: Clear sections and bullets, mostly easy to scan.
levels.4: Clear headings and bullets, short paragraphs, logical order.

categories.name: Specifications and detail
categories.criteria: Does the page give the facts a shopper needs to decide: size, weight, materials, capacity, power, compatibility, what is in the box?

levels.4: Complete specifications with units, including what is in the box and care or compatibility.

categories.name: Claims and trust
categories.criteria: Are claims specific and supportable (numbers, tests, warranty), or vague superlatives and unsupported promises?

levels.2: Mix of supportable and unsupported claims.
levels.4: Specific claims with numbers or conditions; no unsupported superlatives.

categories.name: Search keyword coverage
categories.criteria: Would a shopper searching for this kind of product find it? Are the natural search terms present without stuffing?

levels.0: Almost none of the natural search terms.
levels.1: A few terms, mostly brand-specific words.
levels.2: Main term present, related terms missing.
levels.3: Main and related terms present, natural wording.
levels.4: Main, related and use-case terms present, natural wording, no stuffing.

consistencyRules.message: A page with strong specifications is unlikely to be unstructured; check the structure score.
